newsitem.title: UK: IBCA rates Bank Slaski long-term BBB.
newsitem.headline: IBCA rates Bank Slaski long-term BBB.

text.p: IBCA, the European credit rating agency, said on Tuesday it had assigned a long-term rating of BBB, a short-term of A3, an individual of C and a legal rating of 2 to Bank Slaski w Katowicach.
"BSK is one of nine regional banks formed in 1989 from the breakup of the National Bank of Poland's commercial activities," IBCA said in a statement.
"Although initially wholly-owned by the state, the Dutch banking group ING has gradually acquired a majority shareholding."

IBCA said the bank's long-term rating, which has been set at the current sovereign ceiling for Poland, reflected the credit enhancement factor provided by its major shareholder ING, which it presently rates AA.
The agnecy said Bank Slaski was establishing branches nationwide but its original region is Silesia, an area of long-established heavy industries.
"The bank is closely connected with these industries, whose performance and prospects are very mixed," it said.

"(The bank's) individual rating of C reflects the considerable progress made in reducing impaired lending, a strong local franchise in both corporate and retail business, above average profitability and improving management controls," IBCA added.
